title: Majority Element
category: Array • Hash Table • Divide and Conquer

description.text: Given an array nums of size n, return the majority element. The majority element is the element that appears more than n / 2 times. You may assume that the majority element always exists in the array.
notes: The majority element always exists in the array.
Try Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm for O(1) space solution.
A simple hash map approach works too but uses O(n) space.

examples.explanation: 3 appears 2 times out of 3 elements which is more than n/2 = 1.5.
2 appears 4 times out of 7 elements which is more than n/2 = 3.5.

constraints: The majority element always exists in the array

description.text: Given an integer array nums, move all 0's to the end of it while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements. Note that you must do this in-place without making a copy of the array.
notes: You must modify the array in-place.
The relative order of non-zero elements must be maintained.
Use two pointers — one for current position and one for the next non-zero placement position.

examples.explanation: All zeroes moved to end while maintaining order of 1, 3, 12.
Single zero element stays as is.

inputCode.python:
import json
nums = [0,1,0,3,12]
moveZeroes(nums)
print(json.dumps(nums, separators=(',',':')))

import json
nums = [0]
moveZeroes(nums)
print(json.dumps(nums, separators=(',',':')))

import json
nums = [1,2,3]
moveZeroes(nums)
print(json.dumps(nums, separators=(',',':')))

import json
nums = [0,0,0]
moveZeroes(nums)
print(json.dumps(nums, separators=(',',':')))

import json
nums = [1,2,3,0]
moveZeroes(nums)
print(json.dumps(nums, separators=(',',':')))

notes: Think of it as peeling the outer layer of the matrix one at a time.

title: Longest Common Prefix

description.text: Write a function to find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings. If there is no common prefix, return an empty string "".
notes: Compare characters column by column across all strings.
Stop as soon as a mismatch is found or any string runs out of characters.
If the input array is empty return an empty string.

examples.explanation: The longest common prefix among all three strings is 'fl'.
There is no common prefix among the input strings so return empty string.

constraints: strs[i] consists of only lowercase English letters

description.text: Given an integer array nums, rotate the array to the right by k steps, where k is non-negative. You must do this in-place with O(1) extra space.
notes: If k is greater than the array length, use k % nums.length to get effective rotations.
A clean trick: reverse the whole array, then reverse first k elements, then reverse remaining elements.
You must modify the array in-place.

inputCode.python:
import json
nums = [1,2,3,4,5,6,7]
rotate(nums, 3)
print(json.dumps(nums, separators=(',',':')))

import json
nums = [-1,-100,3,99]
rotate(nums, 2)
print(json.dumps(nums, separators=(',',':')))

import json
nums = [1,2,3]
rotate(nums, 3)
print(json.dumps(nums, separators=(',',':')))

hiddenTestCases.description: k equals array length — no change

inputCode.python:
import json
nums = [1,2,3,4]
rotate(nums, 0)
print(json.dumps(nums, separators=(',',':')))

import json
nums = [1,2,3]
rotate(nums, 5)
print(json.dumps(nums, separators=(',',':')))

description.text: You are a professional robber planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has a certain amount of money stashed. The only constraint stopping you from robbing each of them is that adjacent houses have security systems connected and it will automatically contact the police if two adjacent houses were broken into on the same night. Given an integer array nums representing the amount of money of each house, return the maximum amount of money you can rob tonight without alerting the police.
notes: You cannot rob two adjacent houses.
Think about whether to rob the current house or skip it.
Use dynamic programming: at each step decide to rob current + best from two steps ago, or skip and take best from one step ago.

examples.explanation: Rob house 1 (money=1) then rob house 3 (money=3). Total = 1 + 3 = 4.
Rob house 1 (money=2), house 3 (money=9), and house 5 (money=1). Total = 2 + 9 + 1 = 12.

title: Linked List Cycle
category: Linked List • Two Pointers • Hash Table

description.text: Given head, the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it. There is a cycle in a linked list if there is some node in the list that can be reached again by continuously following the next pointer. Return true if there is a cycle in the linked list. Otherwise, return false.
notes: Use Floyd's Cycle Detection Algorithm (fast and slow pointers) for O(1) space.
A slow pointer moves one step at a time, a fast pointer moves two steps.
If they ever meet, there is a cycle. If fast reaches null, there is no cycle.

examples.explanation: There is a cycle in the linked list where the tail connects to the 1st node (0-indexed).
There is a cycle where the tail connects to the 0th node.
There is no cycle in the linked list.

constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4]
pos is -1 or a valid index in the linked list

hiddenTestCases.description: Cycle present — tail connects to index 1

inputCode.cpp:
Solution sol;
cout << sol.hasCycle(nullptr) << endl;
inputCode.java:
Solution sol = new Solution();
System.out.println(sol.hasCycle(null));

title: Product of Array Except Self

description.text: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i]. The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and without using the division operation.
notes: You cannot use division.
Think about prefix products and suffix products.
answer[i] = product of all elements to the LEFT of i × product of all elements to the RIGHT of i.

examples.explanation: Any position where 0 exists in the array makes all other positions 0.

constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

description.text: Suppose an array of length n sorted in ascending order is rotated between 1 and n times. Given the sorted rotated array nums of unique elements, return the minimum element of this array. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(log n) time.
notes: You must use binary search to achieve O(log n).
The minimum element is the point where the rotation happened.
If nums[mid] > nums[right], the minimum is in the right half. Otherwise it is in the left half including mid.

examples.explanation: The original array was [1,2,3,4,5] rotated 3 times. Minimum is 1.
The original array was [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] rotated 4 times. Minimum is 0.
The original array was [11,13,15,17] rotated 4 times (no rotation). Minimum is 11.

constraints: All integers in nums are unique
nums is sorted and rotated between 1 and n times

description.text: You are given an integer array coins representing coins of different denominations and an integer amount representing a total amount of money. Return the fewest number of coins that you need to make up that amount. If that amount of money cannot be made up by any combination of the coins, return -1. You may assume that you have an infinite number of each kind of coin.
notes: You have unlimited supply of each coin denomination.
Use dynamic programming — build up solutions from smaller amounts to the target.
dp[i] = minimum coins needed to make amount i.
If no combination can make the amount, return -1.

examples.explanation: 11 = 5 + 5 + 1. Three coins needed.
Amount 3 cannot be made with only coin denomination 2.
Amount 0 requires 0 coins.
